promise.title: Your outings, your stories, your video.
body: Wherever you are, close to home or on the other side of the world, whether you are contemplative, hiking solo, into sport a little or a lot, sometimes a bit wild, or simply with family or friends, LGS1920 Studio is made for you.

overview.title: What is LGS1920 Studio?
intro: LGS1920 Studio lets you revisit an outing from its GPS track. Explore the terrain in your browser, mark the places that mattered, and tell the story in a video, a snapshot or a report.

highlights.title: Import and review journeys
highlights.body: Import journeys and tracks, then keep the working state in the browser.

highlights.title: Global 3D scene
highlights.body: Switch between map layers and center the camera on the relevant route context.

highlights.title: Prepare a video
highlights.body: Add POIs, change map layers, add colors, and choose different widgets. Everything remains editable to suit your needs.

highlights.title: Export and share
highlights.body: Final videos can be shared directly on your social networks or saved wherever you like.

privacy.title: Your privacy comes first.
privacy.lead: For now, all data handled by Studio stays in your browser, including videos while they are being processed. Your data can already be synchronized locally across your devices. In a future version, Studio may also allow you to synchronize your data with your own cloud storage, if you choose to do so.

quote.text: You can access your journeys without creating an online account. Studio does not track your activity or use cookies.
quote.closing: If you’d like to show us your outing, share it with #LGS1920Studio.
quote.partnerNote: Using Studio for a public event? You can add us as a partner. It would be great for us and help more people discover LGS1920 Studio. Thank you.

features.title: The main workflows Studio already covers.

cards.title: Journey and track editing
cards.body: Load journeys, edit metadata, tune visibility, and manage track presentation in a consistent way.

cards.title: POI workflows
cards.body: Create, focus, rotate, and keep point-centric views across both POIs and journey-level targets.

cards.title: 3D scene control
cards.body: Move into the 3D scene, track the active camera target, and keep navigation clear.

cards.title: Widgets and overlays
cards.body: Compose visible context with metrics, labels, and supporting panels.

cards.title: Media export
cards.body: Capture screenshots, record videos, and share them with the same visible overlays used in the editor.

cards.title: Journey reports
cards.body: Generate PDF reports or ZIP-packaged HTML reports with metadata, statistics, POIs, coordinates, altitude data, and map captures.

workflow.title: Tell the story of a hike from trailhead to summit.

steps.title: Find your route
steps.body: Import the GPX from your hike. Centre the map on the track to see where the trail leaves the valley and reaches the ridge.

steps.title: Mark the summit
steps.body: Add a point of interest at the summit and give it a name. Show the elevation profile so viewers can follow the climb as they watch the terrain.

steps.title: Save the view
steps.body: Frame the ridge and replay the track to check that the summit stays in view. Record a video or keep a snapshot of your favourite viewpoint.

items.title: 1.0: Current Studio
items.body: A privacy-first, local-first geospatial editor for journeys, tracks, POIs, 2D/3D scenes, camera controls, widgets, replay, snapshots, video, and PDF or HTML journey reports.

items.title: 1.1: Extended activity imports
items.body:
Add FIT and TCX imports from Garmin and Strava while preserving activity and sensor data, with optional authenticated Strava access and connected-provider project files.
Enrich POIs with several looks to fit your designs.

items.title: 1.2: Timeline video editor
items.body: Replace the separate Replay start, replay, and stop controls with a track-based timeline that combines journey replay, clips, and widgets.

items.title: 1.3: 3D camera path editor
items.body: Create editable 3D camera paths with GPS positions, altitude, duration, motion profiles, look-at targets, easing, and optional 360-degree moves.

access.title: Studio is free to use.
access.note: Edit your outdoor adventures, replay scenes, and export videos or reports without a paid subscription.

cards.title: Free today and tomorrow
cards.body:
Studio is free to use today and will remain free to use. There is no paid plan, subscription, or activation fee. Studio gives you access to more than 30 free basemaps.
Unlike many other apps, video creation is completely free, with no limits other than those of your device.

cards.title: Optional freemium or paid assets
cards.body:
You can also use external map and data assets from freemium or paid providers, such as Cesium (Google 3D, Google Maps, etc.), MapTiler, and more.
These services are optional and billed by their own providers. Studio offers them to enrich your videos but has no commercial relationship of any kind with these providers.

faq.title: Common questions about Studio and the public site.

items.summary: Why LGS1920? What does it mean?
items.body: LGS1920 stands for La Grande Sure, a 1,920-metre summit in the Chartreuse massif, in the French Alps, at GPS coordinates 45°20′07″ N, 5°42′11″ E (45.3353, 5.7031).
items.bodyAfter: It is a mountain that means a great deal to me: it is part of my family roots, and I was barely twelve when I climbed it for the first time with my family. At the time, it was my Mont Blanc — better still, my Everest.
items.bodyFinal: One of Studio’s journey samples is, appropriately, named LGS1920. It is one of my favourite hikes, and I still hike it once a year, 54 years later.
